resources.string: Flint uses Android Accessibility to detect which app is in the foreground using app and screen class names, and read web addresses from known browser address bars for website blocking. Not all browsers or pages expose an address. While an enabled Hardcore rule is active, it also reads visible Settings text and content descriptions for its Settings guard. The guard covers known system uninstallers even for other apps, and Flint-related uninstall, force-stop, clear-data and Accessibility-disable screens. If text is unavailable, a recognized App-info or Accessibility screen may be covered even for another app. The guard has no break or Emergency Pass action, works only while Accessibility is running, and may miss screens on some devices or languages. First end or disable active Hardcore rules inside Flint before turning this service off in Android Settings; native Timers have a hold-to-end control. This data is used only to enforce your blocks, stays on your device, and is never sent off your device, shared, or sold. No account or analytics.
